When it comes to display technology, we're reaching a plateau of "it's good enough".

Meaning, 4K doesn't matter. Sure, it's being peddled in stores at the moment, but the truth is that for every increase in resolution, the next increase becomes less significant. 4K is to 1080p what 1440p is to 720p. It's four times as many pixels and thereby four times as much detail.

The problem is that that just doesn't matter. It's not significant enough of an improvement over 1080p to make it worthwhile to upgrade to on it's own. We have to need it for something specific. 720p to 1080p was much more noticeable and it was less pixels overall of an increase both in numbers and percentage.

That's just an example of how we've reached a point of "good enough" in regards to image quality.

My point is, technology is reaching a point where you can get good video quality from a phone. Perfect or "what you'd get from a several thousand dollar setup"? No, but more than "good enough".
